purpose: Evidence and deployment gates for capability items that cannot be implemented safely from the repository alone.

groups.title: Legacy and proprietary JDBC drivers
sharedEvidence: An authoritative support matrix naming the database/server release, exact JDBC driver release, Java 8 support, and driver class
A legally obtained driver archive plus license and redistribution/deployment decision
SHA-256 inventory and Java class-file bytecode scan for every supplied archive
A TLS and authentication profile that does not place secrets in the JDBC URL
A disposable acceptance endpoint with least-privilege read and separately approved write identities
Redacted fixtures covering metadata discovery, bounded reads, prepared writes where in scope, cancellation, timeout, and vendor error handling
promotionCriteria: All shared evidence is attached and approved
The exact driver loads and connects on the EBX Java 8 runtime
Bounded catalog, read, timeout, and cancellation tests pass
Any write operation is separately authorized and proves transaction rollback and affected-row bounds
License, vulnerability, and deployment reviews record an explicit accept decision

specificEvidence: Decision whether the requirement is JDBC database access or bounded DBF-file ingestion; these are different contracts
Authoritative standalone Type-4 Java 8 contract; a bridge or desktop-only driver is not sufficient
Vendor-supported driver/server/Java 8 compatibility statement for the selected deployment
Pinned vendor-supported Java 8 driver release and its deployment documentation
Maintained Java 8 driver support decision and a threat model for local or shared database files
Maintained authoritative Type-4 Java 8 driver contract
Chosen proprietary driver archive, Java 8 bytecode result, and matching server support statement
One exact supported driver family selected, with its URL, driver-class, TLS, and server-version contract
Exact Java 8 vendor driver release, class, URL contract, and matching server support statement
Vendor support and security commitment for a Java 8-compatible driver, or an approved runtime-upgrade decision

rejectionConditions: Only a download URL, marketing page, community forum, or unpinned latest driver is supplied
The archive requires a Java runtime newer than the deployed EBX runtime
The license decision, checksums, TLS behavior, or acceptance endpoint is missing

groups.title: Parquet dependency and schema closure
sharedEvidence: A target use case stating read, write, or both; file origin; expected volume; and supported storage transport
An approved Java 8-compatible dependency lock including all transitive artifacts, licenses, checksums, bytecode levels, and vulnerability disposition
A schema contract for nested values, nullability, decimals, timestamps, dates, binary values, logical types, and schema evolution
Limits for compressed bytes, expanded bytes, rows, row groups, columns, nesting depth, and per-value size
Representative valid, malformed, adversarial, and platform-produced redacted fixtures
promotionCriteria: The complete dependency closure passes license, bytecode, and vulnerability review
The codec rejects oversized or malformed inputs before unbounded allocation
Round-trip and compatibility tests pass for every approved logical type
The provider remains absent unless the complete approved runtime closure is installed

specificEvidence: Named target producer and consumer versions plus golden files generated by those platforms

rejectionConditions: Only top-level library coordinates are supplied without a transitive lock
The intended schema semantics or bounded-input policy is unspecified
Fixtures are synthetic only and do not include files from the target platform

groups.title: Licensed REST integrations and social search
sharedEvidence: An entitled, versioned API specification or licensed customer reference
A sandbox tenant and acceptance credentials stored through the approved secret mechanism
Authentication, token renewal, scopes, pagination, rate-limit, retry, and error-envelope contracts
Redacted request and response fixtures for success, empty result, pagination, throttling, authorization failure, and server failure
Permitted-use, provenance, retention, deletion, and redistribution decisions
An operation allowlist with explicit record, page, payload, timeout, and retry bounds
promotionCriteria: The licensed contract and terms are reviewed for the exact entitled product tier
Sandbox tests prove authentication renewal, bounds, throttling, error redaction, and audit evidence
A governed generic REST template is preferred unless stable product semantics require a dedicated type
No production connector type is registered until live acceptance is signed off

specificEvidence: HCP/HCO entity schemas, identifiers, permitted attributes, matching semantics, and permitted-use decision
Entitled company/contact schemas, match semantics, credit consumption, provenance, and retention behavior
Approved product priority, selected API tier, query and result contract, content-retention rules, deletion handling, and acceptance credentials

rejectionConditions: Endpoints, fields, pagination, or limits would need to be guessed
Only public marketing material or an interactive UI is available
Terms do not permit the intended storage, enrichment, redistribution, or retention behavior
Acceptance requires production credentials or unredacted personal data
